correctness.rationale: The inner vertices of GP(6,2) are exactly the triangle vertices; the others induce the outer six-cycle, and each inner vertex is determined by its spoke. Thus the action described really is the full twelve-element simultaneous dihedral action. A flag has distinct matching ranks, and if two points of one closed flag simplex are identified by the group their support ranks and barycentric coordinates match. This proves embedded closed cells in the quotient with distinct rank-subflag facets; face deletion gives the signed boundary and the checked free-face removals are topological. Independent reconstruction produced the exact starting dimensions (117,1219,3949,5338,3090,600), then used a different free-face order (6250 pairs rather than the frozen script's 6411) to reach a valid three-dimensional core (68,447,838,460). Collapse counts and cores are order-dependent; starting counts and homotopy invariants agree. Orienting each remaining edge low to high rank gives the relator low–mid, mid–high, inverse low–high after the tree is contracted. The independent replay gives a connected tree and eliminates all 380 non-tree generators using reversible defining-relation moves; the resulting π1 is trivial. Signed integral unit-pivot cancellation checks boundary-square and gives (67,380,458) pivots, reducing to one zero-chain and two three-chains with zero differential. Each ±1 pivot splits off a contractible two-term integral summand, so the conclusion is torsion-free, not a field-rank inference. The space is simply connected and H_2=0, thus two-connected by Hurewicz. Two S³ maps giving an integral basis of H_3 now give a homotopy equivalence by homological Whitehead.
residual_risks: The replay independently proves the final invariant, not the line-by-line order of the source's 6411-pair queue. It covers only the finite geometric orbit complex specified in the finding, not a family of generalized Petersen graphs or all subgroups.

value.rationale: Full automorphism-group quotient of the ordinary matching complex is a natural fixed target, with a previously known rational rank that leaves an actual integral question. The result identifies the exact integral homotopy type and rules out quotient torsion; this is especially meaningful in light of the same graph's cyclic quotient with 3-torsion. A researcher comparing subgroup orbit topology can use the exact full-group type. The value is not predicated on arbitrary collapse counts or a separate novelty claim for simple connectivity.
